source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The Chandler campus publishes 169 MW of IT capacity across eight facilities, ranking it the largest published data center footprint in Arizona and representing one-third of the state's 512 MW of published capacity. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, 169 MW of IT load translates to roughly 4,200 racks, though published specifications do not state whether this campus is configured or marketed for AI workloads specifically. The 2 million square feet of technical space accommodates this capacity at a density typical of modern colocation facilities.

The campus holds certifications for security, compliance, and standards required by financial services, healthcare, and government tenants, as well as environmental management, but the operator's published page does not name which workloads or customers currently occupy the site or whether capacity is available. Arizona's grid, which serves Chandler, is not published in the state context; power availability and cost relative to other regions are not specified here and would need separate research.

This campus matters to AI scaling if its capacity is being consumed by accelerator-dense workloads and if Arizona's power supply can sustain further growth. With 57 mapped facilities across the state but only four publishing megawatt figures, Chandler's transparency makes it a useful reference point for the state's infrastructure, but the state's total published capacity of 512 MW remains small relative to major AI hub regions, and the pipeline for additional capacity in Arizona is not documented here.
